html:
Tigranes the Great was king of Armenia from about 95 to 55 BCE, who briefly made it the strongest state east of Rome, stretching from the Caspian to the Mediterranean.

Held as a hostage by the Parthians in his youth, he bought his throne with land. He then took Parthian territory, Syria from the dying Seleucids and parts of Cilicia, called himself king of kings and built a new capital, Tigranocerta, filled with deported Greeks and others. His alliance with his father in law, Mithridates of Pontus, drew him into war with Rome. Lucullus took Tigranocerta in 69 BCE, and in 66 BCE Tigranes submitted to Pompey, keeping Armenia as a Roman ally. He is a central figure of Armenian national memory.
sum: Tigranes the Great was king of Armenia from about 95 to 55 BCE, who briefly made it the strongest state east of Rome, stretching from the Caspian to the Mediterranean.
